protein: DDX3X, the DEAD-box RNA helicase 3 X-linked
readout: Day 15 combined log fold change in variant abundance
assay_method: Saturation genome editing of the endogenous DDX3X locus in HAP1 cells: sgRNA-directed cuts repaired from an HDR template library carrying every designed variant, with variant abundance read by amplicon sequencing at five timepoints. Damaging variants reduce viability and are depleted. The readout is the Day 15 combined log fold change, combining the two independent sgRNA experiments per exon by weighted mean.
remark: The reference sequence is UniProt O00571 unmodified, against which all 7,631 nucleotide-level missense annotations verify at offset 0 using the source's own Protein_position, ref_aa and alt_aa columns. The source is a nucleotide-variant table, so it is collapsed to the 3861 distinct amino-acid substitutions it encodes; 3681 of them are measured more than once because the design adds a redundant, typically multinucleotide, variant for each coding SNV, and those are averaged. That redundancy is the assay's own concordance check and its disagreement is real: the widest spread is L392R at 5.73 log fold change. The WT row is the mean of the 1684 synonymous variants, which the library carries within each exon as its internal controls; they span -4.866 to 0.858 and their mean of -0.0010 sits essentially at zero. Day 15 is the timepoint the paper's own significance calls rest on, and it correlates at r = 0.995 with the LFC-trend score across all timepoints, which is therefore not carried separately. Not extracted from this paper: the 442 stop-gained, 625 inframe-deletion, 1,222 intron, 737 splice-region and remaining non-coding variants, none of which is a substitution this format can express; the Day 7, 11 and 21 timepoints and the LFC-trend, which measure the same variants at a different or aggregated point; and Supplementary Data S1 to S6, which are PheWAS results, machine-learning classifier performance, in-silico predictor comparisons and modelled clinical-classification impact, all computed on top of this same score rather than measured.
